records.name: Directors Gathering
records.summary: A free network for theatre directors in and around Philadelphia. It holds salons and gatherings, mostly on Zoom with some in person, where directors talk about their craft and try out new work.
records.what_you_do: Join a free salon or gathering, or sign up for the free membership to get the digital resource hub and the monthly newsletter about directing opportunities.

schedule.text: Free salons and gatherings, held on Zoom and sometimes in person in Philadelphia. Each one is announced separately.

cost.text: Membership is free. The salons and gatherings listed for 2026 are free. Some events ask for an RSVP.

access.notes: A March 2025 online event has a recording with auto-generated captions.

first_step.how: Sign up for the free membership through the sign-up button on directorsgathering.org, then register for the next salon or gathering on the events page.
first_step.basis: Membership and events are free and open to theatre artists at any career stage, through a public sign-up form; the pages name no application or approval step.
first_step.what_to_expect: Salons usually run about 90 minutes online, with a facilitator who opens the conversation. Gatherings can include a guest artist or a short presentation, and the in-person ones open with about half an hour of food and mingling before the talk. Membership and the listed events are free.
first_visit_tips: Listing times are Eastern Time, and some also give Pacific Time.
Register through the linked form or Eventbrite, since some events ask for an RSVP.
In-person gatherings meet at the CultureWorks Suite, 1315 Walnut St, Suite 300.

records.notes: The site still lists the September 21, 2026 gathering as upcoming, but that date has passed as of today and no later listing was found. Schedule days were removed because the events fall on different weekdays. The 2026 IRS e-postcard names Thomas Snyder as contact; the group's own site names Sisi Wright as executive director, so that name is used. The site shows the email only as an obscured link, so none is recorded. Older pricing for non-members (pay what you decide, $15 suggested) belongs to 2021 and 2022 listings and is not used. Social pages were not read. CultureWorks, which hosts the in-person suite and is the fiscal sponsor, is dropped as a host rather than a group. Philly Latine Theatre Alliance is listed under leads.

records.name: District One Community Education Center
records.summary: The Community Education Center is an arts space on Lancaster Avenue where artists rehearse, teach and perform. It runs dance classes open to the public, a regular open mic and a jazz night, and it rents space to artists and tenant groups.
records.what_you_do: Take a dance class (Funk Sole on Wednesday evenings, a Friday night workshop, or one of the monthly African dance classes), try the open mic, or visit the Blue Grotto, a basement lamp installation open to the public every second Friday.

schedule.text: Weekly: Funk Sole Fundamentals on Wednesdays 6 to 8 pm, and a Friday night workshop at 8 pm. Monthly: African dance classes on the first Thursday, first Saturday, second Saturday and fourth Friday. Every second Friday: the Blue Grotto, 6 to 10 pm, and a jazz night. Every other second Sunday: an open mic, 4 to 9 pm.

cost.text: Dance classes are marked with a dollar sign, but no amounts are listed. Call or email for prices.

first_step.how: Pick a class from the Classes page, then call 215.387.1911 or email Programs@cecarts.org to confirm the start date and the price before your first session.
first_step.basis: The programs page says all levels are welcome in the dance classes, and the center publishes a phone number and email, but the pages do not say how to sign up or whether drop-ins are allowed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Funk Sole Fundamentals runs 6 to 8 pm on Wednesdays, about two hours, and the page says all levels are welcome. The building is a working arts space where artists rehearse and perform, so classes share it with other activity. Prices are not shown online, so ask before you come.
first_visit_tips: Call or email ahead to confirm the class, the price and the start date.
The monthly African dance classes run on different weekends from the weekly classes, so check the day on the programs page.

records.notes: The classes page lists four classes with no amounts. The programs page lists more series that the classes page does not show: an Orisha dance class on second Saturdays, a West African dance class on fourth Fridays, the Blue Grotto, the Outlet open mic and Second Fridays jazz. Two West African listings name different teachers and may be separate classes. The events page lists Monthly Movement Classes on October 10, 2026, from 2 to 4 pm, which is the basis for the sign of life. Kulu Mele, named on the programs page, was fetched: its own site (kulumele.org) gives a 6417 N. 13th Street address and contact details but no class times or prices, and its newest dated item is from 2022, so it is dropped from this batch as a separate group. Accessibility and age rules are not published on any page read. The 2023 copyright footer is not used as evidence.

records.name: Drexel Late Night Series
records.summary: A free weekly open mic night at Drexel's Creese Commuter Lounge, run by students in Drexel's music industry and arts management programs. Performers sign up for five-minute slots in music, comedy, poetry or monologues.
records.what_you_do: Claim a five-minute slot to perform, or come to watch the 8 pm show. Headliners include Drexel students and regional artists.

schedule.text: Every Thursday. Performer sign-ups open at 7:30 pm for the 8 pm show.

first_step.how: Arrive at the Creese Commuter Lounge by 7:30 pm on a Thursday and claim a five-minute slot, or come at 8 pm to watch.
first_step.basis: Anyone interested can claim a slot and the show is open to the public, but the page names no beginner track or first timer welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: The show runs on Thursday evenings, with performers taking five-minute turns in music, comedy, poetry or monologues. Sign-ups open at 7:30 pm, so arrive early if you want a slot. Watching is free and open to all ages.
first_visit_tips: Arrive by 7:30 pm if you plan to perform, since slots are claimed at sign-up.
The show is free, so there is nothing to buy in advance.

records.notes: Neither the upcoming events page nor the full performance calendar lists a dated Late Night Series show, so status stays probably_active with no sign-of-life date. The series page names a university staff member as a contact; that person's direct email and phone are left out, and the general performing arts office email and phone are used instead. The ticket office page returned HTTP 403 and was not read. The copyright year is not treated as evidence.

records.name: EarlyBirds and NightOwls
records.summary: Two run groups, one early morning and one at night, run by Recovery Run Coaching. They run on roads and trails in different parts of the Philadelphia area, and each group posts its own route and time.
records.what_you_do: Join a run with the early morning or night group, after checking that group's posts for the week's route and start time.

cost.text: The site does not list a cost.

first_step.how: Follow the EarlyBirds Instagram page (or NightOwls for the night group) to find the next run's time and place, then show up.
first_step.basis: The coach's site gives no schedule, sign-up steps or first-timer guidance, so the way in is through each group's social media, which is an unclear way in.
first_step.what_to_expect: Runs take place on roads and trails in different spots around the Philadelphia area. The coach's site does not say how long a run lasts, what pace it keeps or what it costs, so ask before your first run.
first_visit_tips: Check the group's Instagram page for the route and start time before you leave home.
Email the coach to ask about pace and cost before your first run.

records.notes: Recovery Run Coaching runs both groups. Its run groups page, about page and contact page give no run times, meeting places, pace, distance, cost or waiver. Run schedules are posted on Instagram, which is a lead-only platform, so no facts were taken from it, and the schedule and location fields are left empty. The contact page gives the email only. Because this is a coaching business's run club, the reviewer may want to confirm that it counts as a community program.

records.name: East Falls River Landing Friends Group
records.summary: A volunteer-led Friends group for the East Falls River Landing, a public boat launch on the Schuylkill River at Kelly Drive in East Fairmount Park. The East Falls Development Corporation helped form the group and still supports it.
records.what_you_do: Help with volunteer days at the landing, which the group holds with Parks and Recreation and the Fairmount Park Conservancy. Ask the group how to join the next one.

locations.label: River Landing (canoe launch and parking lot)

access.notes: The landing is described as an ADA-accessible public facility, with parking in a lot beside it, a portable toilet and a picnic area.

first_step.how: Email efrlfg@gmail.com and ask to be added to the list for the next volunteer day at the landing.
first_step.basis: Volunteer days are open to neighbors, but no schedule or sign-up page was found, so the way in is by email and is not clearly marked.
first_step.what_to_expect: Volunteer days at the landing are work sessions with neighbors and partners such as Parks and Recreation and the Fairmount Park Conservancy. No page we could read gives the dates, the length or what to bring, so ask the group before you come.
first_visit_tips: The lot's listing warns that a left turn into it from westbound Kelly Drive is often hard and is not allowed on weekdays from 4 to 6:30 pm, so plan to approach from the other direction at those times.
Confirm the meeting spot and the time by email before you come.

records.notes: The group has no website of its own. Its only web presence found is a Facebook page, which was not read, so no facts were taken from it. The efrlfg@gmail.com address comes from the East Falls Development Corporation's landing page, which names it as the Friends group's email; the City stewardship email from tier 1 (pprstewardship@phila.gov) is still a route in. The 4530 and 4455 Kelly Drive addresses both appear for the same landing; 4530 is kept because the City list and the development corporation's page use it. The 2026-10 date comes from the City's Friends group list, not from a dated activity post, so status was lowered to probably_active and the date should be checked. The development corporation page also has a Join Now form that does not say which group it is for, so it is not used. The one web search found no dated activity by the group in the past year. Partners named on the landing pages (Fairmount Park Conservancy, Schuylkill River Greenways, PowerCorpsPHL, Audubon Discovery Center, Delaware Valley Ornithological Club, Circuit Trails Coalition, William Penn Foundation, PA Fish and Boat Commission) are funders, builders, agencies or institutions rather than Friends groups, so they are dropped from this batch.

records.name: Ebenezer Maxwell Mansion
records.summary: A Victorian house museum in Germantown that shows nineteenth century home life through its rooms, gardens and collections. It also runs guided tours, Victorian theatre, lectures, book clubs and family events, and it looks for volunteers in tours, collections and events.
records.what_you_do: Take a guided house tour on a weekend, see a Victorian theatre show or a free family event, or volunteer as a tour guide or helper through the museum's volunteer form.

schedule.text: Tours run Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays at noon, 1, 2 and 3 pm. Thursday tours are by advance reservation only.

cost.text: Guided tours are $10 per person. Some events are free and others have their own prices.

access.notes: The house is fully air conditioned, according to the visit page.

first_step.how: Reserve a Friday, Saturday or Sunday tour at noon, 1, 2 or 3 pm on the museum's online ticketing page; reservations are appreciated.
first_step.basis: Public weekend tours need no application, and the museum trains its tour guides and says no professional historian background is needed to volunteer.
first_step.what_to_expect: A tour takes you through the rooms of the Victorian house, and the gardens around it are open to stroll. Guides are trained by the museum, so you do not need a history background to lead one. A tour costs $10 per person, and reservations are appreciated.
first_visit_tips: Book on the online ticketing page; groups of six or more can book any day by phone or email.
The Thursday tours need an advance reservation, so do not arrive without one.

records.notes: Tour days conflict between pages: the visit page's main text lists Thursday tours at noon, 1 and 2 pm, while the homepage and the visit sidebar list Friday to Sunday at noon, 1, 2 and 3 pm, with Thursdays by reservation only; the record follows the homepage. The October 2026 events on the homepage (Historic Germantown Second Saturday on October 10, the Sleepy Hollow play on October 23 to 25, Trick or Treating on October 31) carry no year, and the events page shows no upcoming events, so the 2026-10 sign of life is carried from tier 1 and is not confirmed by a dated line. The executive director's name replaces the contact name carried from tier 1, per the site. A volunteer page publishes a director's personal email, which is left out. The proposed Victorian Society Philadelphia Chapter is a plan the museum would host, not a group taking members, so it is dropped from this batch. Historic Germantown's shared OnePass ticket is a ticket pass, not a group, and is dropped. Several menu links on the staff and Black History pages point to unrelated gambling sites and were skipped.

records.name: EgoPo Classic Theatre
records.summary: A Philadelphia theater company that stages its own productions each season. Single tickets, subscriptions and memberships let people see the season's shows, and volunteers help with productions and public events.
records.what_you_do: See a show by buying a single ticket, a subscription or a membership, which adds tickets and a drink package. Volunteers help with productions and public events, and the page lists free concessions and free tickets as perks.

schedule.text: Each season has a few productions, each with a limited run, and the dates are posted on the website.

locations.label: Carpenters' Hall (performance venue named on the parking page)

cost.text: Basic Subscription $80. Memberships are $150 (Bronze), $300 (Silver) and $500 (Gold). Single-ticket prices are not listed on the site.

first_step.how: Buy a single ticket for a show on the Buy Tickets page of the EgoPo website, or start with the $80 Basic Subscription, which includes one ticket each to three shows.
first_step.basis: Anyone can buy a ticket to a public show, and volunteers can reach the company through a contact sheet on its site.
first_step.what_to_expect: A visit is a night at the theater for one of the season's limited runs. Some shows have few tickets, and subscribers get priority on those, so buy early. Memberships start at $80, and single-ticket prices are not listed on the site.
first_visit_tips: For Company, the page says you may bring a blanket, pillows and pajamas, which are optional.
The box office is open Monday to Friday, 10 am to 4 pm, and from 10 am to 2 pm in the week of a performance.
Shows can be held at other venues, so check the venue for each show before you go.

records.notes: The tier 1 location (317 Dickinson Street) is the company's office, and the parking page says every performance is held elsewhere; the record now lists the office and Carpenters' Hall at 320 Chestnut St, which the parking page names for one production. The parking page's transit paragraph names the Fifth Street Market-Frankford stop and several bus routes but mentions another theater, so no stop is recorded. No page read gives accessibility, age or late arrival rules, and the volunteer page names no age or time requirement. The homepage names Rowan University and TITX as co-producers, and the parking page names Theatre Exile in a transit sentence; these are an institution, a co-producer and another company rather than community groups that take members, so they are dropped from this batch.

notes: All 7 batch groups got a deep pass: homepage plus up to four or five joining, classes, visit, volunteer, events or contact pages each. 29 fetches in total (one returned 403) and 1 WebSearch, used for East Falls River Landing, which has no website of its own. Facebook and Instagram were never read for facts. Status changes: East Falls lowered from active to probably_active because the 2026-10 date comes from a City registry, not an activity post. Directors Gathering's September 21, 2026 gathering has passed as of today and no later date is listed. EgoPo's tier 1 location was the office and is corrected. Contact names for Directors Gathering and Ebenezer Maxwell Mansion now follow the names on their own sites. Kulu Mele was fetched and dropped as a record in this batch (noted under the CEC record). Other partner organizations were dropped with reasons in the individual notes. Search budget: 1 of 1 used. No rate limiting was seen.
